p1.key: 3.0 mol C2H3Cl would need 7.5 mol O2, so O2 is limiting. CO2 : O2 = 4 : 5, so n(CO2) = 3.0 × 4/5 = 2.4 mol.
As4 + 5O2 → As4O10 (10 O atoms need 5 O2). The reactant coefficients add up to 1 + 5 = 6.
n(CH4) = 1.6/16 = 0.10 mol, so 0.20 mol O2 is needed. Mass = 0.20 × 32 = 6.4 g.
Gas volumes are in the same ratio as moles: 10 dm3 SO2 needs 5 dm3 O2. Air is only 20 % O2, so the volume of air = 5/0.20 = 25 dm3. 5 dm3 is the oxygen alone.
n(CaCO3) = n(CO2) = 0.15 mol, so mass of pure CaCO3 = 0.15 × 100 = 15 g. Purity = 15/20 × 100 = 75 %.
With v = 2: C balance gives x = 4, Cl gives z = 2, H (6 atoms) gives y = 2. Oxygen on the right = 8 + 2 = 10 atoms, so w = 5.
H2 and Cl2 react 1 : 1, so 1.5 mol Cl2 is limiting. It reacts with 1.5 mol H2 (leaving 0.5 mol H2) and forms 2 × 1.5 = 3.0 mol HCl.
H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> + 2NaOH, so n(acid) = ½ × 36.2 × 0.225/1000. Dividing by 25.0/1000 dm<sup>3</sup> gives c = 36.2 × 0.225/(2 × 25.0). B wrongly doubles instead of halving.
H3PO4 + 2NaOH → Na2HPO4 + 2H2O. n(H3PO4) = 0.0100 × 0.200 = 2.00 × 10−3 mol, so n(NaOH) = 4.00 × 10−3 mol and V = 4.00 × 10−3/0.200 = 0.0200 dm3 = 20.0 cm3.
Balanced: 2PbS + 3O2 → 2PbO + 2SO2. Sum of coefficients = 2 + 3 + 2 + 2 = 9.

n(Zn) = 3.25/65.4 ≈ 0.050 mol; n(Cu<sup>2+</sup>) = 0.100 dm<sup>3</sup> × 0.25 mol dm<sup>−3</sup> = 0.025 mol. They react 1 : 1, so Cu<sup>2+</sup> is limiting: all Cu<sup>2+</sup> reacts and about 0.025 mol Zn is left over.

Cu + 2Ag<sup>+</sup> → Cu<sup>2+</sup> + 2Ag. n(Cu) = 6.4/63.5 ≈ 0.10 mol; n(Ag<sup>+</sup>) = 0.10 × 1.0 = 0.10 mol, which reacts with only 0.05 mol Cu. Ag<sup>+</sup> is limiting, so excess copper remains.
n(CaC2) = 64 000 g / 64 g mol−1 = 1000 mol, giving 1000 mol C2H2 → 1000 mol C2H4 units. Mass of polyethene = 1000 × 28 g = 28 kg.
56.0 g N2 = 2.00 mol, so in theory 4.00 mol NH3 = 68.0 g. Yield = 34.0/68.0 × 100 = 50%.

p1.key: C3H8 + 5O2 → 3CO2 + 4H2O. The products contain 3 × 2 + 4 × 1 = 10 O atoms, so 5 O2 are needed.
n(C4H10) = 58 g ÷ 58 g mol−1 = 1.0 mol. The ratio C4H10 : CO2 = 2 : 8 = 1 : 4, so 4 mol CO2 form.
6.0 mol Fe2O3 would need 18 mol C, but only 9.0 mol is present, so carbon is limiting. 9.0 mol C gives 9.0 × 2/3 = 6.0 mol Fe.
The mole ratio C4H10 : CO2 = 2 : 8 = 1 : 4, so 3 mol butane gives 3 × 4 = 12 mol CO2.
C3H8 + 5O2 → 3CO2 + 4H2O. The product coefficients total 3 + 4 = 7.
2PbS + 3O2 → 2PbO + 2SO2. The products contain 2 + 4 = 6 O atoms, so 3 O2 are needed.
CO2 + 3H2 → CH3OH + H2O. 2 mol CO2 would need 6 mol H2, so H2 is limiting: 3 mol H2 gives 3/3 = 1 mol methanol.
n(CaCO3) = 50 ÷ 100 = 0.50 mol, so theoretical CaO = 0.50 × 56 = 28 g. Yield = 7 ÷ 28 × 100 = 25 %. Always compare masses of the same product.
Balanced: 2Na + 2H2O → 2NaOH + H2. Coefficients 2 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 7 (the "1" in front of H2 counts).
Each SO4²⁻ gives one BaSO4, so n(SO4²⁻) = 5.02 × 10⁻³ mol. The formula has 2 SO4²⁻ per Fe, so n(Fe) = 5.02 × 10⁻³ ÷ 2 = 2.51 × 10⁻³ mol.

The amount of CO2 depends on the amount of CaCO3 (both acids react completely), so the same volume forms. Ethanoic acid reacts more slowly because it is weak and has a higher pH (fewer H⁺), so A is wrong.
For gases at the same T and p, volume ratio = mole ratio. C2H2 : O2 = 2 : 5, so V(O2) = 0.40 × 5/2 = 1.0 dm³.
C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>4</sub> + 4O<sub>2</sub> → 3CO<sub>2</sub> + 2H<sub>2</sub>O. Oxygen atoms needed: 3 × 2 + 2 × 1 = 8, so 4 O<sub>2</sub>.
2C4H10 + 13O2 → 8CO2 + 10H2O. With whole numbers the O2 coefficient is 13 (for one C4H10 it would be 6½).
80 t ÷ 160 = 0.5 "tonne-moles" of Fe2O3, giving 2 × 0.5 = 1.0 of Fe. Mass = 1.0 × 56 = 56 tonnes. A forgets the 2 : 1 ratio.
n(H2SO4) = 0.0300 × 0.200 = 6.00 × 10⁻³ mol; 2KOH + H2SO4, so n(KOH) = 1.20 × 10⁻² mol. V = 1.20 × 10⁻² ÷ 0.800 = 0.0150 dm³ = 15.0 cm³. A forgets the 2 : 1 ratio.
Balanced: Fe2O3 + 3C → 2Fe + 3CO. n(Fe2O3) = 1600/160 = 10 kmol, which needs 30 kmol C, but only 144/12 = 12 kmol C is present, so carbon is limiting. Fe = 12 × 2/3 = 8 kmol × 56 = 448 kg.
MnO2 + 4HCl → MnCl2 + Cl2 + 2H2O. Four Cl are needed on the right (2 in MnCl2, 2 in Cl2), so 4HCl; the 4 H then make 2H2O, which also balances the two O atoms. C.
C2H4 + 3O2 → 2CO2 + 2H2O. n(C2H4) = 7.00/28.1 mol, so n(CO2) = 2 × 7.00/28.1 mol; volume = 2 × 22.4 × 7.00/28.1 dm3. B forgets the 1 : 2 mole ratio.
Sulfuric acid is diprotic: H2SO4 + 2NaOH, so it needs twice the volume (40 cm3). The others are monoprotic and each need 20 cm3. Acid strength does not matter for the amount needed. B.
2H2 + O2 → 2H2O. 5 O2 react with 10 H2, giving 10 H2O and leaving 2 H2 in excess (oxygen is limiting). Only diagram A shows 10 water molecules plus 2 H2 molecules, with all atoms conserved.
From the equation, 4 mol Al react with 3 mol O2. n(O2) = 6.0 × 3/4 = 4.5 mol.
2 mol Al give 3 mol H2, so 3 mol Al give 4.5 mol H2. Mass = 4.5 mol × 2.0 g mol⁻¹ = 9.0 g. Answer B (4.5) is the moles, not the mass.
Balanced: 2C2H2 + 5O2 → 4CO2 + 2H2O. Sum of coefficients = 2 + 5 + 4 + 2 = 13.
10.0 mol C2H3Cl would need 25.0 mol O2, so O2 is limiting. 5 mol O2 give 2 mol H2O, so 10.0 mol O2 give 4.00 mol H2O.
Balanced: Fe2O3 + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO2. Sum of coefficients = 1 + 3 + 2 + 3 = 9.
n(HCl) = 0.100 dm³ × 1.0 mol dm⁻³ = 0.10 mol, but 0.10 mol CaCO3 needs 0.20 mol HCl, so HCl is limiting. 2 mol HCl → 1 mol CaCl2, so yield = 0.050 mol.
Balanced: 4C3H5N3O9 → 12CO2 + 10H2O + 6N2 + O2. Check O: 4 × 9 = 36 = 24 + 10 + 2. The coefficient of nitroglycerine is 4.
n(Fe2O3) = 80 g ÷ 159.7 g mol−1 ≈ 0.50 mol. The ratio Fe2O3 : CO2 is 1 : 3, so 1.5 mol CO2 × 44 g mol−1 = 66 g.

Gas volumes react in the mole ratio C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>2</sub> : H<sub>2</sub> = 1 : 2, so 3.0 dm<sup>3</sup> H<sub>2</sub> is limiting and reacts with only 1.5 dm<sup>3</sup> C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>2</sub>, giving 1.5 dm<sup>3</sup> C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub>.
Balanced equation: 4NH<sub>3</sub> + 5O<sub>2</sub> → 4NO + 6H<sub>2</sub>O. Check: N 4 = 4, H 12 = 12, O 10 = 4 + 6. So the ratio NH<sub>3</sub> : O<sub>2</sub> = 4 : 5.
Volume ratios equal mole ratios. 50 cm3 CxHy gives 200 cm3 CO2, so x = 4, and 250 cm3 H2O, so 5 H2O per molecule and y = 10. The formula is C4H10.
n(CaCO3) = 5.0 g ÷ 100.09 g mol−1 = 0.050 mol. The ratio is 1 : 1, so 0.050 mol CO2 × 44.01 g mol−1 = 2.2 g. A gives the amount in mol, not the mass.
n(HCl) = 0.100 dm3 × 2.00 mol dm−3 = 0.200 mol. 2HCl gives 1H2, so 0.100 mol H2 is formed. Volume = 0.100 mol × 22.4 dm3 mol−1 = 2.24 dm3.

Balanced equation: Ca<sub>3</sub>(PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>2</sub> + 3H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> → 3CaSO<sub>4</sub> + 2H<sub>3</sub>PO<sub>4</sub>. The 3 Ca need 3 SO<sub>4</sub>, and the 2 PO<sub>4</sub> give 2 H<sub>3</sub>PO<sub>4</sub>. Check: H 6 = 6.
n(BaCl2) = 0.1000 dm3 × 0.50 mol dm−3 = 0.050 mol. n(Na2SO4) = 0.0500 dm3 × 0.10 mol dm−3 = 0.0050 mol. The ratio is 1 : 1, so Na2SO4 is limiting and 0.0050 mol BaSO4 forms.
n(O2) = 2.4 ÷ 24 = 0.10 mol. From the equation 2 mol NaBrO3 give 3 mol O2, so n(NaBrO3) = 0.10 × 2/3 = 0.067 mol.
n(NaOH) = 4.0 ÷ 40.00 = 0.10 mol; n(H2SO4) = 0.10 × 1.0 = 0.10 mol. 0.10 mol NaOH reacts with only 0.050 mol H2SO4, so 0.050 mol H2SO4 is in excess and only 0.050 mol Na2SO4 forms (B wrong).
CxHy + (x + y/4)O2 → xCO2 + (y/2)H2O. Sum = 1 + (x + y/4) + x + y/2 = 1 + 2x + 3y/4.

Complete combustion needs O2 : propene = 9 : 2 = 4.5 : 1 by volume. 1 dm3 propene needs 4.5 dm3 O2, so 4 dm3 is insufficient and CO forms. A (10 vs 9), B (2.3 vs 2.25) and D (14 vs 13.5) all have enough oxygen.
2NaOH + H2SO4: 0.10 mol H2SO4 needs 0.20 mol NaOH, so with only 0.10 mol NaOH, NaOH runs out first. A is stoichiometric; NaOH : HNO3 is 1 : 1, so in C HNO3 is limiting and D is exact.
n(NaOH) = 2 × 0.050 = 0.100 mol. V = n/c = 0.100 ÷ 0.20 = 0.500 dm3 = 500 cm3. Option B (0.50) is the volume in dm3, not cm3.
6.0 mol CO reacts with only 6.0 ÷ 3 = 2.0 mol Fe2O3, so CO is limiting and 5.0 − 2.0 = 3.0 mol Fe2O3 remains unreacted.
n(Mg) = 0.30 ÷ 24.31 mol, and the 1 : 1 ratio gives the same amount of H2. V = n × 22.7, so V = 0.30 × 22.7 ÷ 24.31 dm3. Option A wrongly doubles the amount using the HCl coefficient.
Balanced: 2C8H18 + 17O2 → 16CO + 18H2O (C: 16; H: 36; O: 16 + 18 = 34). Sum = 2 + 17 + 16 + 18 = 53. 26.5 is the sum with a fractional coefficient for O2, which the question rules out.
n(CaCO3) = 1.00 ÷ 100.00 = 0.0100 mol needs 0.0200 mol HCl, but 0.0400 mol HCl is present, so CaCO3 is limiting. n(CO2) = 0.0100 mol, so V = (1.00 ÷ 100.00) × 22.7 dm3.
n(NaOH) = 0.0500 × 0.120 = 6.00 × 10−3 mol. H2SO4 is diprotic: 0.0250 × 0.120 × 2 = 6.00 × 10−3 mol H+. B and D supply only 3.00 × 10−3 mol H+, and A gives 3.0 × 10−3 mol.
Theoretical yield = (7 ÷ 28) × 46 g. % yield = actual ÷ theoretical × 100 = 6 ÷ (7 × 46 ÷ 28) × 100 = (6 × 28 × 100) ÷ (7 × 46).
Percentage yield = actual moles ÷ theoretical moles × 100. Ethanol → ethene is 1:1, so theoretical n = 5.0/46 and actual n = 2.0/28: yield = (2.0/28) ÷ (5.0/46) × 100.
n(SO2) = 32 ÷ 64 = 0.50 mol. From the equation, 4 FeS2 give 8 SO2 (1 : 2), so n(FeS2) = 0.50 ÷ 2 = 0.25 mol.
Equal gas volumes contain equal moles. 1 dm3 CH4 needs 2 dm3 O2, so O2 is limiting. 1 dm3 O2 reacts with 0.5 dm3 CH4, giving 0.5 dm3 CO2.
From the equation, 2 NH3 form with 3 Mg(OH)2, a ratio of 2 : 3. n(Mg(OH)2) = 0.50 × 3/2 = 0.75 mol.
Balanced: 2C3H6 + 9O2 → 6CO2 + 6H2O (using C3H6 + 4½O2, then doubling to get integers). Sum = 2 + 9 + 6 + 6 = 23.
0.10 mol CaCO3 would need 0.20 mol HCl, but only 0.10 mol is present, so HCl is limiting. The ratio HCl : CO2 is 2 : 1, so the maximum CO2 = 0.10 ÷ 2 = 0.05 mol.
Balanced: MnO2 + 4HCl → MnCl2 + 2H2O + Cl2. Four Cl atoms are needed: two in MnCl2 and two in Cl2. Sum = 1 + 4 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 9.
HCl is limiting: 0.10 mol HCl needs only 0.05 mol Mg (0.20 mol present). Mole ratio HCl : H2 = 2 : 1, so maximum H2 = 0.10/2 = 0.05 mol.
Sn(OH)4 + 2NaOH → Na2SnO3 + 3H2O. Coefficients 1 + 2 + 1 + 3 = 7.
